# Task App CRM — Technical Reference

**Last reviewed:** 2026-05-23
**Source:** Generated by direct inspection of the current codebase.

This document is the authoritative reference for server-side architecture used by connected Task App CRM targets. The product is offline-first, not offline-only: the offline-web artifact remains a standalone local deployment, while the enterprise-web PWA and Dataverse targets use target-specific adapters and services around the same shared core UI in `packages/core/src/`.

For offline-web technical details, see `apps/offline-web/README.md` and the current agent guidance in `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`.

## 1. Server Overview

The server backs the enterprise-web PWA target. Offline-web and Dataverse builds do not require this server. The server also serves the enterprise SPA static assets (`dist/enterprise/`) when `ENTERPRISE_STATIC_DIR` is set.

| Item          | Value                                                         |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Framework     | Hono v4 (`@hono/node-server` adapter)                         |
| Language      | TypeScript strict mode (`noImplicitAny`, `strictNullChecks`)  |
| Module format | ESM (`"type":"module"`); all imports use `.js` extensions     |
| Database      | PostgreSQL via Drizzle ORM (`drizzle-orm/pg-core`)            |
| Auth IdP      | Microsoft Entra ID (OIDC + PKCE, JWKS validation via `jose`)  |
| Policy engine | OPA (REST sidecar → WASM → in-process fallback)               |
| KMS           | Azure Key Vault (`@azure/keyvault-keys`)                      |
| Observability | OpenTelemetry (`@opentelemetry/sdk-node`, OTLP HTTP exporter) |
| Entry point   | `server/src/index.ts`                                         |

---

## 2. Entry Point & Middleware Stack

**`server/src/index.ts`**

OTel `init()` must run before any other import that creates spans or metrics. Imports follow via dynamic `import()` statements after OTel init.

Middleware execution order per request:

```
1. CORS headers / OPTIONS preflight  (server/src/middleware/cors.ts)
2. Connection counter increment/decrement  (inline, metrics.ts)
3. OTel root span  (server/src/observability/middleware.ts)
4. Auth middleware — /api/v1/* only  (server/src/auth/middleware.ts)
5. Route handler + opaMiddleware(action) per route
```

**Public routes** (no auth): `GET /healthz`, `GET /readyz`

**Graceful shutdown** — `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT`:

1. `stopDestructionScheduler(timer)` — stop KMS poll loop
2. `closeDb()` — drain pg pool
3. `process.exit(0)`

**CORS** — `ALLOW_ORIGINS` env var; comma-separated whitelist; no wildcards; rejects origins not on the list.

## 3. Database Schema

Schema files: `server/src/db/schema/`

### 3.1 Pre-existing tables (migrations 0000–0001)

| Table               | Primary key type | Tenant column                                                     |
| ------------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tenant_users`      | `uuid`           | `org_id uuid`; Entra mapping uses `entra_tenant_id + external_id` |
| `audit_events`      | `uuid`           | `org_id uuid`                                                     |
| `kms_key_lifecycle` | `uuid`           | `org_id uuid`                                                     |

RLS on pre-existing tables uses `app.org_id` session variable.

### 3.2 CRM entity tables (migration 0002)

All 14 CRM tables share: `text id PK`, `text tenant_id NOT NULL`, `timestamptz created_at`, `timestamptz updated_at`, `timestamptz deleted_at` (nullable — soft delete).

| Table              | Notable columns                                                                                                       |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `clients`          | `name`, `contact_name`, `email`, `phone`, `description`, `stage` (enum: Prospect/Active/Inactive/Churned)             |
| `departments`      | `name`, `description`                                                                                                 |
| `projects`         | `name`, `description`, `client_id`, `owner_id`, `dept_id`, `stage`, `priority`, `due_date`, `start_date`, `narrative` |
| `tasks`            | `title`, `description`, `project_id`, `assignee_id`, `status`, `priority`, `due_date`, `done`                         |
| `people`           | `name`, `role`, `email`, `phone`, `dept_id`, `client_id`                                                              |
| `tags`             | `name`, `color`                                                                                                       |
| `communications`   | `type`, `body`, `client_id`, `project_id`, `person_id`, `date`, `created_by`                                          |
| `time_entries`     | `task_id`, `description`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, `running`, `duration_seconds`, `created_by`                       |
| `notifications`    | `title`, `body`, `type`, `related_id`, `read`, `user_id`                                                              |
| `files`            | `name`, `size`, `mime`, `storage_url`, `client_id`, `project_id`, `created_by`                                        |
| `documents`        | `title`, `content`, `excerpt`, `section`, `pinned`, `created_by`                                                      |
| `standalone_notes` | `body`, `created_by`                                                                                                  |
| `conversations`    | `title`, `model_id`, `messages` (jsonb), `user_id`                                                                    |
| `legal_holds`      | `user_id`, `tenant_id`, `reason`, `placed_at`, `expires_at`, `lifted_at`, `placed_by`, `lifted_by`                    |

### 3.3 Row-Level Security

Every CRM table has:

```sql
ALTER TABLE <table> ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON <table>
  USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id', true)::text);
CREATE POLICY tenant_insert ON <table> FOR INSERT
  WITH CHECK (tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id', true)::text);
```

### 3.4 KMS append-only trigger

`kms_key_lifecycle` rows can never be updated — a `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger (`prevent_kms_key_update`) raises an exception to enforce the append-only invariant.

### 3.5 Tenant isolation helper

**`withTenant<T>(tenantId, fn)`** in `server/src/services/base.ts`:

```ts
db.transaction(async (tx) => {
  await tx.execute(sql`SET LOCAL app.tenant_id = ${tenantId}`)
  return fn(tx)
})
```

All service methods call this wrapper. Queries outside a `withTenant` transaction will fail RLS checks unless the session variable is set by other means.

## 4. Service Layer

All service files: `server/src/services/`

### 4.1 Common pattern

Each entity service exports: `list`, `getById`, `create`, `update`, `delete`. All use `withTenant()`. All mutating operations (`create`, `update`, `delete`, `suspend`, `erase`) call `writeAuditEvent()` from `base.ts`.

```ts
export async function create(tenantId: string, userId: string, data: CreateInput): Promise<Entity> {
  return withTenant(tenantId, async (tx) => {
    const [row] = await tx.insert(table).values({ ...data, tenantId, createdBy: userId }).returning()
    await writeAuditEvent({ tenantId, userId, eventType: 'entity.created', ... })
    return row
  })
}
```

### 4.2 Special service behaviours

| Service                    | Special behaviour                                                             |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tasks.service.ts`         | `list()` accepts `overdue` / `dueToday` filter flags                          |
| `documents.service.ts`     | `create()` and `update()` auto-compute `excerpt` (first 200 chars of content) |
| `conversations.service.ts` | Exports `appendMessage(tenantId, id, message)` in addition to CRUD            |
| `audit.service.ts`         | Exports `exportNdjson()` and `exportCsv()` for streaming audit log exports    |
| `users.service.ts`         | Exports `suspend(tenantId, userId, requestedBy)` — sets `suspended_at`        |

### 4.3 Audit event writer

**`writeAuditEvent(input)`** in `base.ts` inserts into `audit_events`. Maps `tenantId → orgId` (same UUID value; column name differs between old and new tables). Returns the new audit event `id`.

## 5. Route Handlers

All route files: `server/src/api/routes/`

### 5.1 Common pattern

```ts
const router = new Hono()

const CreateSchema = z.object({ name: z.string().min(1), ... })

router.post('/', opaMiddleware('create'), async (c) => {
  const tenantId = c.get('tenantId') as string
  const userId   = c.get('userId')   as string
  const parsed   = CreateSchema.safeParse(await c.req.json())
  if (!parsed.success) return c.json({ error: parsed.error.issues }, 400)
  const result = await createEntity(tenantId, userId, parsed.data)
  return c.json(result, 201)
})
```

Rules:

- Never expose stack traces or raw DB error messages in HTTP responses
- Always return `{ error: 'Internal server error' }` on unexpected errors (status 500)
- Always return `{ error: parsed.error.issues }` on Zod failures (status 400)
- `GET /` routes support `?page=`, `?pageSize=` via `paginationValues()` from `base.ts`

### 5.2 Special routes

| Route              | Method | Path                                 | Notes                                    |
| ------------------ | ------ | ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| `audit.ts`         | GET    | `/api/v1/audit/export`               | Streams NDJSON or CSV; `?format=csv`     |
| `conversations.ts` | POST   | `/api/v1/conversations/:id/messages` | Appends a message to conversation        |
| `admin.ts`         | POST   | `/api/v1/admin/users/:id/suspend`    | Requires `admin` role via OPA            |
| `admin.ts`         | POST   | `/api/v1/admin/users/:id/erase`      | GDPR erasure; calls `runErasureWorkflow` |

## 6. Auth — OIDC + PKCE

Production auth is fail-closed:

- `server/src/auth/middleware.ts` requires an active `tenant_users` row matching both Entra `oid` (`external_id`) and Entra `tid` (`entra_tenant_id`).
- The server never treats Entra `tid` as the internal tenant. It maps the IdP tenant boundary to internal `tenant_users.org_id`.
- `server/src/auth/state-store.ts` stores PKCE state and refresh-token replay/revocation state in Redis for production. Non-production memory state exists only for local/test use.
- PKCE state is single-use and expires after 10 minutes. Refresh tokens are tracked by SHA-256 hash only.
- Production startup validates `DATABASE_URL`, Entra/OIDC config, allowed origins, Redis state stores, and Key Vault config in `server/src/config/production.ts`.

**`server/src/auth/oidc-service.ts`** — `OidcServiceImpl`:

| Method                                     | Purpose                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `buildAuthorizationUrl(state, pkce)`       | Constructs Entra ID authorize URL with S256 code challenge                   |
| `exchangeCodeForToken(code, codeVerifier)` | POSTs to token endpoint; returns `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `id_token` |
| `validateToken(token)`                     | `createRemoteJWKSet` + `jwtVerify` via `jose`; validates `iss`, `aud`, `exp` |
| `rotateRefreshToken(refreshToken)`         | `grant_type=refresh_token`                                                   |
| `revokeToken(token)`                       | POSTs to logout endpoint                                                     |

**`generatePkceAsync()`** — exported helper; uses `crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256')` for the S256 challenge.

**`server/src/auth/middleware.ts`** — `authMiddleware`:

1. Reads `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
2. Calls `validateEntraIdToken(token)` from `oidc.ts`
3. Looks up user in `tenant_users` by `sub` claim
4. Sets `c.set('userId')`, `c.set('tenantId')`, `c.set('role')`
5. Returns `401` on any failure — never leaks error details

---

## 7. Authorization — OPA

**`server/src/middleware/opa.ts`** — `opaMiddleware(action: string)`:

Evaluation chain (first success wins):

1. **REST sidecar** — `POST ${OPA_URL}/v1/data/crm/allow` with `{ input: { role, tenantId, action, resourceTenantId } }`
2. **WASM** — `@open-policy-agent/opa-wasm`; loads `policies/crm.wasm` lazily (compile with `opa build crm.rego`)
3. **In-process TypeScript fallback** — role-based logic matching the Rego policy

**`server/policies/crm.rego`** policy summary:

| Role             | Allowed actions                                                    |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `admin`, `owner` | All actions including `suspend_user`, `erase_user`, `manage_users` |
| `editor`         | `read`, `create`, `update`                                         |
| `viewer`         | `read` only                                                        |

Cross-tenant deny: if `input.resourceTenantId` is set and differs from `input.tenantId`, the request is denied regardless of role.

## 8. Observability — OpenTelemetry

### 8.1 Initialisation

`OtelServiceImpl.init()` in `server/src/observability/otel.ts` must run before any other import. Configures:

- `NodeSDK` with `@opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node`
- `OTLPTraceExporter` (HTTP) — endpoint from `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`

### 8.2 Request middleware

`otelMiddleware` in `server/src/observability/middleware.ts`:

- Starts an active OTel span per request
- Sets span attributes: `http.method`, `http.route`, `http.status_code`, `tenant.id`
- Injects `X-Trace-Id` response header
- Records span error on 5xx responses

### 8.3 Metrics

`server/src/observability/metrics.ts`:

| Metric                     | Type             | Description                                   |
| -------------------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `crm.requests.total`       | Counter          | All requests, labelled by method/route/status |
| `crm.requests.duration_ms` | Histogram        | Request latency                               |
| `crm.connections.active`   | Observable gauge | In-flight requests                            |

Helper: `recordRequest(method, route, status, durationMs)` — called by `otelMiddleware`.

### 8.4 Structured logging

`otel.log({ timestamp, level, service, tenantId, requestId, message, extra? })` — writes JSON to stdout. All server components use this; never `console.log`.

## 9. KMS / GDPR

### 9.1 Key lifecycle

`server/src/kms/key-service.ts` — `AzureKeyVaultKeyService`:

- Uses `@azure/keyvault-keys` + `@azure/identity` DefaultAzureCredential
- `scheduleKeyDestruction(userId, tenantId, effectiveAt)` — inserts `SCHEDULE_DESTRUCTION` row into `kms_key_lifecycle`
- `getKeyUri(userId)` — returns vault URI for the user's per-user KEK

Key naming convention: `tktaskapp-user-<userId>`

### 9.2 Legal hold

`server/src/kms/legal-hold.ts` — `LegalHoldService`:

| Method                                                       | Purpose                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `placeHold(userId, tenantId, reason, expiresAt?, placedBy?)` | Inserts active hold                                                                  |
| `liftHold(holdId, liftedBy)`                                 | Sets `lifted_at`                                                                     |
| `isUserOnHold(userId)`                                       | Returns `true` if `lifted_at IS NULL AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > now())` |

### 9.3 Erasure workflow

`server/src/kms/erasure-workflow.ts` — `runErasureWorkflow(userId, tenantId, requestedBy)`:

1. `isUserOnHold(userId)` — throws `LegalHoldActiveError` if active hold exists
2. `scheduleKeyDestruction()` — schedules Azure KV key deletion (if `AZURE_KV_URL` set)
3. `Promise.allSettled([...])` — soft-deletes rows across all CRM tables where `userId` appears
4. `writeAuditEvent({ eventType: 'gdpr_erasure_requested' })` — immutable audit record
5. Returns `{ userId, status: 'scheduled', effectiveAt, auditEventId }`

### 9.4 Destruction scheduler

`server/src/kms/destruction-scheduler.ts`:

- Polls `kms_key_lifecycle` every 60 seconds
- For each row with `event = 'SCHEDULE_DESTRUCTION'` and `effective_at <= now()`:
  - Skips if a `DESTROYED` row already exists for the same `key_vault_uri`
  - Calls `beginDeleteKey(keyName).pollUntilDone()` on Azure KV
  - Inserts `DESTROYED` lifecycle row (append-only)
  - Writes `kms_key.destroyed` audit event
- `startDestructionScheduler()` → `NodeJS.Timeout`; `stopDestructionScheduler(timer)` — called on graceful shutdown

## 10. AI Gateway

`server/src/ai-gateway/policy-engine.ts` — `evaluateAiGatewayRequest(request)`:

Checks in order:

1. **Model allowlist** — set of approved model IDs (`claude-*`, `gpt-4o*`, `gemini-1.5-*`)
2. **Per-user rate limit** — 20 RPM sliding window; Redis (`ioredis`) if `AI_GATEWAY_REDIS_URL` is set, else in-memory `Map`
3. **Per-tenant monthly budget** — default 1,000,000 tokens; configurable via `AI_GATEWAY_MONTHLY_BUDGET_TOKENS`; Redis-backed in multi-instance deployments
4. **PII scrubbing** — regex patterns for email, credit card, SSN, UK NI number; detected PII redacted to `[REDACTED-TYPE]`; request is allowed but `sanitisedMessage` is returned instead of the original

All check failures write an audit event via `db.insert(auditEvents)`. `_auditLog` catches and logs errors to stderr — never blocks the request.

## 12. Developer Workflows

### Running the server

```bash
cd server
cp .env.example .env          # fill in credentials
pnpm install
pnpm db:validate              # verify committed SQL migration integrity
pnpm db:migrate               # apply all migrations
pnpm db:seed                  # optional: dev seed data
pnpm dev                      # tsx watch
```

### Building OPA WASM (optional — in-process fallback works without it)

```bash
cd server
opa build -t wasm -e crm/allow policies/crm.rego -o policies/crm.wasm
```

### Running migrations in production

```bash
cd server && pnpm db:migrate
```

Drizzle applies only unapplied migrations from `server/drizzle/`. The migration history is tracked in the `__drizzle_migrations` table.

Production migrations are committed SQL artifacts. The repository does not install
`drizzle-kit` or run migration generation in CI because production deployment must
consume deterministic, reviewed SQL. Schema changes must update `server/drizzle/*.sql`
and `server/drizzle/meta/_journal.json`, then pass `pnpm run validate:migrations`.

### Adding a new CRM entity

1. Create `server/src/db/schema/<entity>.ts` — Drizzle table definition with `tenantId`, `deletedAt`
2. Export from `server/src/db/schema/index.ts`
3. Add a new ordered SQL migration in `server/drizzle/` and journal entry in `server/drizzle/meta/_journal.json`
4. Include `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, tenant policies, indexes, and rollback notes in the migration review
5. Create `server/src/services/<entity>.service.ts` with `list`, `getById`, `create`, `update`, `delete`
6. Create `server/src/api/routes/<entity>.ts` Hono router; add `opaMiddleware(action)` per route
7. Mount router in `server/src/index.ts`: `app.route('/api/v1/<entity>', <entity>Router)`

### Security checklist for new routes

- [ ] `opaMiddleware(action)` on every handler
- [ ] Zod schema validation; return `400` on failure
- [ ] `withTenant()` wrapping every DB query
- [ ] `writeAuditEvent()` on every mutating operation
- [ ] No raw error details in HTTP responses
